messages:
incidentbot: Pager fired: HIGH • inference-gateway.prod-usw2 — 5xx rate jump to 6.3% (5m). Alert rule: gateway.5xx_rate > 5%

pagerduty-bot: PD: Incident INC-12345 created and routed to the on-call alias @alex. Escalation policy: 2m -> @kyle -> 5m -> team fallback. Link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/INC-12345

alex: acked — heading in. First pass: are we seeing a deployment or infra blip? :rotating_light:

kyle: I see spike across multiple worker pools. Not just one AZ. Metrics look like increased 502/504s from grpc-proxy layer.

maya: adding logs from edge (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T02:14:22Z inference-gw edge-23 502 "upstream reset by peer" route=/v1/generate user_id=...
2026-03-15T02:14:23Z inference-gw edge-19 502 "context deadline" route=/v1/embeddings
```

emily: customer impact check: synthetic canaries showing ~2% fail rate for api/v1/generate in prod-usw2; error spike concentrated on requests > 1024 tokens.

sebastian: that's probably KV cache pressure + connection churn. Recent canary bumped kvsize to 1.2GB per shard, maybe causing evictions.

alex: ok — quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce per-request concurrency to the gateway for long requests, 2) route long-requests to warm pool, 3) roll back KV size tweak if it correlates. I'll try (1) first.

kyle: how to reduce concurrency quickly? gate config toggle or traffic-slice?

alex: gate config is feature-flagged. Running: `curl -X POST https://cfg.internal/flags/gateway.long_request_concurrency -d '{"value":8}'` — will push global.

maya: while you're toggling, I'm going to force a warmup on the dedicated warm pool for long seq by priming a few model instances. Running: `kubectl exec -n infra gateway-warmup -- /scripts/prime_long.sh`

incidentbot: Action logged: alex changed flag gateway.long_request_concurrency -> 8 (was 24).

pagerduty-bot: PD: Acknowledgement recorded for INC-12345 by alex at 2026-03-15T02:16:10Z

emily: short-term customer note: adding a post to status page in case it persists. Draft: "We are investigating increased 5xx for generation requests in US-WEST2, some customers may see transient failures for long-context requests." Shall I publish?

alex: yes, publish with note that engineers are mitigating, ETA TBD. :+1:

sebastian: after the flag change I'm seeing 5xx drop to ~3.1% over the next 90s. Latency slightly higher for head requests but throughput steadier.

kyle: good signal. still seeing tails. Maya — any errors in model pods?

maya: model pods show repeated `OOM_kvcache` warnings on a subset of nodes. Logs: `WARN kv_cache: evicting 40MB shard due to memory_pressure`. Rolling back the kvsize tweak should stop immediate evictions.

alex: can we rollback config? Is it a feature flag or deployment?

maya: kvsize came from a ConfigMap that was updated in the canary yesterday `kv-config.v2`. I'll patch the configmap to previous: `kubectl apply -f kv-config-v1.yaml` and then rollout restart for gateway pods.

sebastian: recommend doing a rolling restart of the affected nodepool/shard rather than full gateway — minimize churn.

alex: executing rollback now.

incidentbot: Action logged: maya applied kv-config-v1 and started rolling restart on gateway shards shard-a, shard-b.

pagerduty-bot: PD: INC-12345 status updated => Mitigating (acknowledged)

kyle: after restart, 5xx rate trending down to ~1.2% over 4 minutes. Still a few spikes. Any downstream retries causing cascade?

emily: customer impact estimate: roughly 18 customers saw elevated error rates (based on alert set) — none are high-value signed-enterprise contracts that reported directly yet. Customer support triaging.

alex: good. Let's keep the mitigation patch in place until tomorrow morning EU window. Create follow-up ticket to test kv-config variants and run a soak.

maya: creating ticket INTG-8723 with details and benchmark script. Adding runbook link: https://runbook.internal/inference/5xx-wave (internal)

sebastian: one more ask — enable extra logging on failed requests for 30m to capture headers and payload sizes. I'll open a short-lived debug job.

alex: done. `kubectl apply -f debug-logging.yaml` — debug enabled for 30m.

incidentbot: Debug job scheduled: debug-logging -> expires in 30m.

pagerduty-bot: PD: INC-12345 note added: mitigation applied (kv rollback + concurrency throttle). Monitoring.

emily: status page updated: "Mitigation in progress, error rates decreasing. Next update in 30m."

kyle: handing off to @emily for overnight watch after 30m check-in. I'll be reachable if it flares.

alex: good handoff. If 5xx remains >1% after 30m we'll consider a regional failover and capacity bump.

emily: I’ll monitor dashboards, slack alerts and PD notifications. Will escalate to @sebastian and @kyle if it crosses threshold.

sebastian: thanks — logging retention for this incident will be extended to 7d for postmortem.

emily: taking baton now. Last bit: anyone want to add customer comms draft? I put a note in the support thread.

alex: added small note re: affected endpoints and suggested retry strategy (exponential backoff).

incidentbot: Thread closed for active edits. Will reopen on PD escalation or manual command",
__notes: This document is a synthetic Slack thread representing an incident coordination conversation. Messages are presented as a single continuous string per agents.md requirements.
